description: Hi, we're Analog Orbit, a small team working on the Flame in Freefall challenge for NASA Space Apps Warangal 2026. We are final-year Aeronautical Engineering student. Working with Python, MATLAB, AutoCAD and ANSYS (CFD), and I'm doing my final-year project on winglets, so I'm comfortable with flow and combustion-style data. We're keeping the scope small and finishing in two days, so you'll get a clear project and something solid to show for your portfolio.
summary: Analog Orbit built AeroGuard, a web prototype for exploring fire behaviour in a microgravity habitat, built with Streamlit and Python. It is designed to help engineers reason about fire-safety margins for spacecraft. The app is linked to NASA PSI MST 2024 n-dodecane combustion test conditions (pressure, droplet diameter, and oxygen fraction) as its data foundation. The app's telemetry, damage, and suppression outputs are simulated, not measured or validated against flight data. We present it as a prototype and list validation against the published paper as our next step.
details: AeroGuard is a Streamlit web app with interactive panels for habitat fire scenarios: material degradation, surface damage, live sensor telemetry, and a 3D flammability view. Tools: Python, Streamlit, pandas, and [plotting library used by your friend]. Our data: NASA PSI MST 2024 test conditions, loaded as a metadata CSV. Goal: make fire-safety scenarios easier to explore and compare, and show clearly which outputs are simulated. Next steps: load the MST_2024_Dext measurement file, plot extinction diameter against pressure and oxygen, and validate against the published paper.
